title: Apple Watch Series 11 breathing-disturbance notifications send a 79-year-old to his cardiologist; morning watch ECGs show AF after “elevated” nights and CPAP starts without polysomnography
summary: Fukuoka case (Cureus, 26 May 2026): sleep-apnoea notifications prompted consultation; watch ECGs showed AF only after “elevated” breathing-disturbance nights; CPAP under way, no polysomnography.
account: Maruyama (Haradoi Hospital, Fukuoka), Hieda and Fukata reported a case in Cureus on 26 May 2026. The consultation is undated. The patient is a 79-year-old Japanese man with hypertension, dyslipidemia, type 2 diabetes and symptomatic paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF). A 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) had documented it a decade earlier. After retirement no paroxysms were documented by ambulatory or standard ECG, and pulsed-field ablation was deferred. Some months after he began wearing an Apple Watch Series 11 paired with an iPhone 15 Pro, he consulted the authors. He asked about notifications of nocturnal “respiratory disturbance”. He activated the watch ECG every morning and evening. AF paroxysms were detected repeatedly on mornings after nights the watch rated breathing disturbance “elevated”. They were not detected after “not elevated” nights, and they terminated by evening. He is undergoing CPAP therapy, and pulsed-field ablation will be considered depending on its effect on the paroxysms. No polysomnography was performed. The authors state that watch-detected breathing disturbance is not equivalent to the apnea-hypopnea index. They state that the watch ECG cannot fully substitute for conventional ECG, and that the notification algorithm “was reportedly developed using advanced machine learning”. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) cleared Apple's Sleep Apnea Notification Feature under 510(k) K240929 on 13 September 2024. Apple's 510(k) submission says that it uses a deep learning algorithm on Apple Watch accelerometer data, analyzed in 30-day windows. It was trained on over 11,000 nights with polysomnography or home sleep-test reference. No treatment outcome is reported.
purpose: The notification feature is built to identify patterns of breathing disturbance suggestive of moderate-to-severe sleep apnea and tell the user. The ECG app is built to record and classify single-lead rhythm. Both were used as designed.
system: Apple Watch Sleep Apnea Notification Feature (breathing-disturbance notifications) and the ECG app
model_version: Apple Watch Series 11 with iPhone 15 Pro

ratings.reason: A man whose AF was thought quiescent learned that paroxysms recur after disturbed-breathing nights, and he started CPAP. No confirmed sleep-apnea diagnosis and no treatment effect are reported.

ai_role.statement: The notification feature's deep-learning model, described in Apple's submission to FDA, flagged elevated breathing disturbance and brought the patient to the clinic. His own morning ECG recordings, read by the authors, showed the AF paroxysms. The paper does not state separately what the ECG app's classifier reported. Clinicians chose CPAP and deferred ablation. The treating authors report the clinical episode. Apple supplies the technical description and validation in its 510(k) summary. FDA's clearance is a separate regulatory decision and does not verify this patient's benefit.

fields.account: Maruyama (Haradoi Hospital, Fukuoka), Hieda and Fukata reported a case in Cureus on 26 May 2026. The consultation is undated. The patient is a 79-year-old Japanese man with hypertension, dyslipidemia, type 2 diabetes and symptomatic paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF). A 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) had documented it a decade earlier. After retirement no paroxysms were documented by ambulatory or standard ECG, and pulsed-field ablation was deferred. Some months after he began wearing an Apple Watch Series 11 paired with an iPhone 15 Pro, he consulted the authors. He asked about notifications of nocturnal “respiratory disturbance”. He activated the watch ECG every morning and evening. AF paroxysms were detected repeatedly on mornings after nights the watch rated breathing disturbance “elevated”. They were not detected after “not elevated” nights, and they terminated by evening. He is undergoing CPAP therapy, and pulsed-field ablation will be considered depending on its effect on the paroxysms. No polysomnography was performed. The authors state that watch-detected breathing disturbance is not equivalent to the apnea-hypopnea index. They state that the watch ECG cannot fully substitute for conventional ECG, and that the notification algorithm “was reportedly developed using advanced machine learning”. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) cleared Apple's Sleep Apnea Notification Feature under 510(k) K240929 on 13 September 2024. Apple's 510(k) submission says that it uses a deep learning algorithm on Apple Watch accelerometer data, analyzed in 30-day windows. It was trained on over 11,000 nights with polysomnography or home sleep-test reference. No treatment outcome is reported.

The patient is a 79-year-old Japanese man with hypertension, dyslipidemia, type 2 diabetes and symptomatic paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF). A 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) had documented it a decade earlier. After retirement no paroxysms were documented by ambulatory or standard ECG, and pulsed-field ablation was deferred. Some months after he began wearing an Apple Watch Series 11 paired with an iPhone 15 Pro, he consulted the authors. He asked about notifications of nocturnal “respiratory disturbance”. He activated the watch ECG every morning and evening. AF paroxysms were detected repeatedly on mornings after nights the watch rated breathing disturbance “elevated”. They were not detected after “not elevated” nights, and they terminated by evening. He is undergoing CPAP therapy, and pulsed-field ablation will be considered depending on its effect on the paroxysms. No polysomnography was performed. The authors state that watch-detected breathing disturbance is not equivalent to the apnea-hypopnea index. They state that the watch ECG cannot fully substitute for conventional ECG, and that the notification algorithm “was reportedly developed using advanced machine learning”. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) cleared Apple's Sleep Apnea Notification Feature under 510(k) K240929 on 13 September 2024. Apple's 510(k) submission says that it uses a deep learning algorithm on Apple Watch accelerometer data, analyzed in 30-day windows. It was trained on over 11,000 nights with polysomnography or home sleep-test reference. No treatment outcome is reported.

produced_by: Nightly watch wear with the sleep-apnea notification feature active, plus the owner's habit of recording a watch ECG every morning and evening
A known history of paroxysmal AF that made the morning traces interpretable to his cardiologists
Access to a clinic willing to act on watch data (CPAP started without polysomnography)
must_hold: The user completes onboarding and wears the watch during sleep, since the feature evaluates 30-day windows opportunistically
Clinicians confirm with conventional ECG and polysomnography, which the authors say the watch cannot replace and which was not done here
